title: Incorrect or missing package comment non-default.
summary: Packages must have a package comment that is formatted according to the guidelines laid out in https://go.dev/wiki/CodeReviewComments#package-comments. It is in Staticcheck since 2019.1. It is in the stylecheck group of checks.

title: Dot imports are discouraged.
summary: Dot imports that aren’t in external test packages are discouraged. It is in Staticcheck since 2019.1. It is in the stylecheck group of checks.

title: Poorly chosen identifier non-default.
summary: Identifiers, such as variable and package names, follow certain rules. It is in Staticcheck since 2019.1. It is in the stylecheck group of checks.

title: Incorrectly formatted error string.
summary: Error strings follow a set of guidelines to ensure uniformity and good composability. It is in Staticcheck since 2019.1. It is in the stylecheck group of checks.

title: Poorly chosen receiver name.
summary: Quoting Go Code Review Comments. It is in Staticcheck since 2019.1. It is in the stylecheck group of checks.

title: A function’s error value should be its last return value.
summary: It is in Staticcheck since 2019.1. It is in the stylecheck group of checks.

title: Poorly chosen name for variable of type time.Duration.
summary: time.Duration values represent an amount of time, which is represented as a count of nanoseconds. An expression like 5 * time.Microsecond yields the value 5000. It is in Staticcheck since 2019.1. It is in the stylecheck group of checks.

title: Poorly chosen name for error variable.
summary: Error variables that are part of an API should be called errFoo or ErrFoo. It is in Staticcheck since 2019.1. It is in the stylecheck group of checks.

title: Should use constants for HTTP error codes, not magic numbers.
summary: HTTP has a tremendous number of status codes. While some of those are well known (200, 400, 404, 500), most of them are not. It is in Staticcheck since 2019.1. It is in the stylecheck group of checks.

title: A switch’s default case should be the first or last case.
summary: Placing the default case at the beginning or end of a switch makes it easier to find and keeps the explicit cases together. An exception is when a fallthrough statement makes the position of the default case significant. It is in Staticcheck since 2019.1. It is in the stylecheck group of checks.

title: Use consistent method receiver names non-default.
summary: Methods on the same type should use the same receiver name, including both pointer and value receivers. Consistent names make it easier to recognize the receiver when reading different methods of the type. It is in Staticcheck since 2019.1. It is in the stylecheck group of checks.

title: Don’t use Yoda conditions.
summary: Yoda conditions are conditions of the kind if 42 == x, where the literal is on the left side of the comparison. These are a common idiom in languages in which assignment is an expression, to avoid bugs of the kind if (x = 42). It is in Staticcheck since 2019.2. It is in the stylecheck group of checks.

title: Avoid zero-width and control characters in string literals.
summary: Invisible format and control characters in string literals can be hard to spot and can make the source code misleading. If such a character is intentional, make it visible with an escape sequence in an interpreted string literal; otherwise, remove it. It is in Staticcheck since 2019.2. It is in the stylecheck group of checks.

title: Importing the same package multiple times.
summary: Go allows importing the same package multiple times, as long as different import aliases are being used. That is, the following bit of code is valid. It is in Staticcheck since 2020.1. It is in the stylecheck group of checks.

title: The documentation of an exported function should start with the function’s name non-default.
summary: Doc comments work best as complete sentences, which allow a wide variety of automated presentations. The first sentence should be a one-sentence summary that starts with the name being declared. It is in Staticcheck since 2020.1. It is in the stylecheck group of checks.

title: The documentation of an exported type should start with type’s name non-default.
summary: Doc comments work best as complete sentences, which allow a wide variety of automated presentations. The first sentence should be a one-sentence summary that starts with the name being declared. It is in Staticcheck since 2020.1. It is in the stylecheck group of checks.

title: The documentation of an exported variable or constant should start with variable’s name non-default.
summary: Doc comments work best as complete sentences, which allow a wide variety of automated presentations. The first sentence should be a one-sentence summary that starts with the name being declared. It is in Staticcheck since 2020.1. It is in the stylecheck group of checks.

title: Redundant type in variable declaration non-default.
summary: In a local variable declaration, omit an explicit type when the initializer already determines the same type. For example, use var x = f() instead of var x T = f() when f returns T. Keep the explicit type when omitting it would change the variable’s type, such as when assigning a concrete value to an interface variable. It is in Staticcheck since 2021.1. It is in the stylecheck group of checks.

title: Check signature of methods of well-known interfaces.
summary: An analyzer of go vet, which runs with go test. Run it alone with go vet -stdmethods.

title: Report uses of too-new standard library symbols.
summary: An analyzer of go vet, which runs with go test. Run it alone with go vet -stdversion.

title: Check for string(int) conversions.
summary: An analyzer of go vet, which runs with go test. Run it alone with go vet -stringintconv.

title: Check that struct field tags conform to reflect.StructTag.Get.
summary: An analyzer of go vet, which runs with go test. Run it alone with go vet -structtag.
